title: Problem using TSAN with NVIDIA GPU on Linux
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible: master

### System information

Linux with NVIDIA GPU

### Issue description

This issue is basically this issues, but inside the Godot repo for easier search, tracking and some Godot specific workarounds:
- https://github.com/google/sanitizers/issues/1647
- https://github.com/google/sanitizers/issues/1678

Currently you can't create a Vulkan device and use TSAN at the same time using NVIDIA GPU. 

Normal workarounds:
1) Use OpenGL, the argument is `--rendering-driver opengl3`;
2) Use Vulkan software rasterizer (like lavapipe);

Editor workarounds:
1) Use OpenGL with a different GPU and manually specify its index `--rendering-driver opengl3 --gpu-index 0`, despite the warning about the GPU index doing nothing, it allows you to open the editor;
2) Use a Vulkan software rasterizer (like lavapipe);

What should work in editor, but currently doesn't:
1) Using `--rendering-driver opengl3` on a different GPU without specifying the `--gpu-index`;
2) Using `--rendering-driver opengl3` on an NVIDIA GPU. Using or not using `--gpu-index` doesn't help here, it will always crash.

Normally just switching to OpenGL should allow you to open the editor even on the NVIDIA GPU, but Godot still creates a Vulkan device for testing in the same process, this is fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120992 . Tbh not sure why it even creates the Vulkan device when using OpenGL, but it does. If the PR is merged, the editor workarounds can be removed. More accurately it's a LightmapGI and Betsy specific problems, so I'm not sure how large the project should also be to be affected.

<details>
<summary>Tested on</summary>

```
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 26.1.5-arch1.1 - Compatibility - Using Device: Intel - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (CFL GT2)
```
```
OpenGL API 3.3.0 NVIDIA 610.43.03 - Compatibility - Using Device: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650
```
</details>

### Steps to reproduce

Compile editor with TSAN and open any project.
